Global Catholic Network Reports From Spain That
"the kind of music youth listen to has a direct effect on the amount of their drug consumption."
Marijuana prohibition is even undermining religious faith.

First, faith and family are not "antidotes to drugs," but rather more like vaccines against the problems that many young people try to escape through substance abuse.

An antidote is something taken after the fact. Of course, this article has a lot of problems distinguishing cause and effect from correlation.

However, the nonsense in this article is precisely the sort of thing that will drive young people away from both faith and family. Bad thinking and hypocrisy not only undermine effective "drug education" but also undermine the credibility of organized religion in the modern world.

Churches are failing in their responsibilities to the young, because they are failing in their responsibilities to the truth.

Marijuana prohibition is even undermining religious faith.)

Australian Article On "Marijuana Addicts" Illustrates How Prohibitionism
Can Interfere With Treatment of People Who Are Truly Cannabis Dependent

From the EWTN Global Catholic Network
editor@cwnews.com
http://www.ewtn.com/
February 1, 1999

Discotheque Music Conducive to Addiction

MADRID, JAN 31 (ZENIT).- According to a study carried out among youth in five European cities by the International Red Cross, religious beliefs and a healthy family environment are key factors against drug addiction. The research also revealed that the kind of music youth listen to has a direct effect on the amount of their drug consumption.

The use of drugs is evidently greater among non-believers and those who do not practice their faith, than among those who have a live religious faith. This was conclusion of research carried out in Coimbra, Portugal; Modena, Italy; Nice, France; Utrecht, Holland and Palma de Mallorca, Spain.
See
New Dutch Drug Use Data Show Success Of Policies of Truth And Tolerance
Full Text of Press Release And Tables With Data On All Drugs

There is also a close relation between drugs and music. In discotheques with "Techno" and "Punk" music the use of drugs is greater than in those with "Pop" and "Salsa."

A report of the Economic and Social Council published in Madrid reveals the disquieting fact that in Madrid one of every four youths younger than 18 years has tried hashish or marijuana; about 44% acknowledge habitual smoking and around 72% drink alcohol in excess at least once a month.

(Marijuananews note: It is not entirely clear from the sentence construction, but it would appear that to them the idea that 25% have tried marijuana is somehow more "disquieting" than that "72% drink alcohol in excess at least once a month." In any case, marijuana use is given first place in their hierarchy.)

The drugs most used by Madrid youth are marijuana and synthetic hallucinogenic drugs, which can be readily obtained in discotheques and on the street, followed by heroin and cocaine.

Last year, 150 people died in Madrid from drugs. Tobacco was the third cause of death in the capital city that same year, claiming over 6,000 lives.

(Marijuananews note: Am I missing something? Like the meaning of the word "drugs" or a sense of proportion. Forty times as many people were killed by tobacco as by all "drugs"combined. Never mind that marijuana did not cause any of those deaths. And what is the music of choice for tobacco users? Gregorian chants?)
